title: Outbox shift notes: two-patch day
body:
2025-11-04 morning shift (08:30-11:00)

Context:
- Rolled two small patches to staging yesterday evening: kv-prefetch heuristic tweak (PR 889) and short-request fast-path (INF-3421). Wanted to validate p95/p99 impact before promoting.
- Brief: some customer workloads with lots of short prompts (<=32 tokens) saw tail latency rise after rolling new batch scheduler defaults.

High-level observations:
- Baseline (pre-patch): p99 ~ 980ms on pool-3 under medium load (50 qps).
- After kv-prefetch tweak only: p99 -> 760ms, p95 -> 220ms. CPU on inference-node +6%, memory unchanged.
- After enabling short-request fast-path: p99 -> 540ms in quick AB test (mixed traffic), but saw occasional 1.4s spikes when host GC coincided with batch flush.

Quick logs / queries I ran:
- grep for request ids that hit fast-path: "rg "fast-path=true" logs/2025-11-03 | head -n 40"
- sample latency distribution per model: "python tools/latency_hist.py --model redwood-v1 --since 2025-11-03"
- traced a 1.4s spike: span shows 200ms kernel lock wait (kv cache eviction) then 900ms token gen.

Hypotheses:
1) The fast-path reduces queueing but increases NF (non-async) work that can collide with GC/evictions, producing occasional large spikes.
2) kv-prefetch reduces retrieval latency but increases background eviction pressure; if eviction occurs while fast-path is doing synchronous IO, we hit kernel locks.

Immediate experiments to run (order matters):
- EXP-1: Run fast-path with jittered GC pauses disabled on a canary node (set ENV INFERENCE_GC_JITTER=0) for 2 hours. Metric: p99, % spikes >1s. (owner: me)
- EXP-2: kv-prefetch conservative mode (prefetch_window=8 -> 4) on same canary; compare eviction rate and kernel lock time. (owner: Lina)
- EXP-3: Add tiny async handoff for short-path: return to scheduler before token-gen heavy IO. Quick prototype in branch sa-handoff-short. (owner: Marcus)

Immediate TODO (today):
1) Push EXP-1 toggle to canary pool-3a (infra ticket INF-3450) - target 09:30 deploy.
2) Add a lightweight metric: "fast_path_sync_time_ms" to telemetry (temporary flag, 1-min resolution).
3) Add a jitter to eviction thread on canary nodes (reduce lock contention).
4) Draft quick postmortem note if spikes persist; include sample traces and timeline.

Notes for debugging next shift:
- Watch for kernel lock traces around kv-eviction: search for "kv_eviction_lock" in traces.
- If p99 improves but p50 worsens, check batching horizon config (we might be dropping batching efficiency).
- Keep an eye on thermals on node-7; yesterday rack reported 74C package under sustained 60 qps for 30m. That's near thermal-throttle threshold for that GPU revision.

Parking lot / non-blocking ideas:
- Evaluate micro-VM isolation for short-path threads to avoid GC collisions (likely medium effort).
- Experiment: pre-warm small request model shards (a la tiny hot cache) to avoid eviction thrash.
- Longer-term: make KV eviction adaptive to current fast-path load.

Links / references:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/889 (kv-prefetch heuristic)
- Jira: INF-3421 (short-request fast-path), INF-3450 (canary deploy toggle)
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime - thread ts 170... (see pinned)

Random scratch items (notes-to-self):
- Remember to keep experiment window small (1-2h) and snapshot telemetry before/after.
- If we see p99 regressions after EXP-2, revert prefetch_window to 8 immediately.
- Capture core dump if we see node OOMs; but shouldn't happen (mem stable yesterday).

End-of-shift quick summary (11:05):
- Rolled EXP-1 schedule for 09:30 (me).
- Lina taking EXP-2 runway.
- Marcus prototyping async handoff; aim to bench by EOD.
- Next update: send short note to #serving-runtime with latency diffs and trace examples.

-- Sahil
